title: JPA Entity Mapping

richText: Entities and tables
An entity is a Java class whose instances JPA stores in a relational database.
JPA means Jakarta Persistence API. It defines mapping annotations and persistence operations. Hibernate is a common implementation.
ORM means object-relational mapping. It describes how Java objects correspond to tables, rows and columns.
@Entity marks an entity class. @Table chooses its table name.
Each entity needs a primary key. @Id marks the Java field or property holding that key.
A JPA entity needs a public or protected no-argument constructor.
Spring Boot 3 uses jakarta.persistence annotations. Older Spring Boot 2 projects use javax.persistence.
Fields and columns
@Column can choose a column name and describe constraints such as nullability.
When @Id is placed on a field, JPA reads and writes fields directly. Getters and setters are not required for that field access.
@Transient excludes a field from persistence.
Database constraints protect stored data. They do not replace validation of incoming requests.
Generated identifiers
@GeneratedValue asks the persistence provider to obtain an identifier using the selected generation strategy.
IDENTITY uses a database identity column. SEQUENCE uses a database sequence. AUTO lets the provider choose a strategy.
Leave a generated identifier unset when creating a new entity.

example.title: Map an employee to a table
description: Use the relational connection from the previous page.
Place Employee.java under the application package so Spring Boot finds the entity.
For this disposable learning database, use ddl-auto=create to generate the table. For a persistent database, create the matching table with a migration.
explanation: Employee maps to employees. One saved Employee represents one row.
id maps to the primary key and receives its value from the identity column.
name is mapped as a required column.
The protected constructor lets JPA create an Employee when reading a row.
The public constructor lets application code create an employee without supplying an ID.
